Body: Just run the installer. Both issues fixed for me.

I hit two more long-session crashes on OpenCode 1.18.18, and these cores identify a concrete Bun 1.3.14 root cause that is related to this issue but different from the original report's decoded stack.

Both processes terminated with `SIGILL` at the same intentional Bun trap:

```text
core 1: thread 870278 frame 0 = opencode.exe + 0x2407064 (VA 0x2607064)
core 2: thread 2313947 frame 0 = opencode.exe + 0x2407064 (VA 0x2607064)
signal: 4 (ILL)
embedded Bun: 1.3.14
OpenCode: 1.18.18
Linux x86-64 baseline
```

That exact `0x2607064` crash address and the surrounding native path match oven-sh/bun#31159:

```text
Bun__JSValue__unprotect
jsc.JSValue.JSValue.unprotect
runtime.webcore.streams.Result.deinit
runtime.webcore.ByteStream.deinit
runtime.webcore.ReadableStream.NewSource(...).decrementCount
runtime.webcore.ReadableStream.NewSource(...).JSReadableStreamSource.finalize
```

Bun fixed this use-after-free in oven-sh/bun#31963, merged as oven-sh/bun@7ff11819c2b75e43d4afd827454f36095d7b4dd0. `StreamError::JSValue` could remain parked in `ByteStream.pending.result` without a GC root; finalization could then unprotect a freed/recycled JS value. The fix roots the value with `jsc::strong::Optional` and adds `test/js/bun/s3/s3-stream-error-gc.test.ts`.

Validation performed locally:

- Bun 1.3.14 reproduces the upstream regression.
- `1.4.0-canary.1+b7a043103` contains the fix and passes the regression test.
- I rebuilt the OpenCode 1.18.18 Linux baseline executable with that canary runtime and resumed both intact sessions.
- The replacement processes have so far completed more than 45 minutes of sustained history replay, streaming, tool calls, GC/compaction, and subagent work without another core dump.

OpenCode's current `dev` branch still pins Bun 1.3.14, and Bun has not yet published a stable release containing `7ff11819`. A stable runtime bump once that release exists should remove this confirmed crash path. I would avoid a canary bump unless maintainers explicitly want one.

References:

- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/31159
- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/31963
- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/7ff11819c2b75e43d4afd827454f36095d7b4dd0

Same root cause here, confirmed from a second browser-hosted deployment (xterm.js over a WebSocket PTY bridge, opencode 1.18.18 on Linux). Just wanted to add the concrete symptom + evidence and confirm the workaround, in case it helps the fix land.

**Symptom:** the stale width doesn't only leave blank space/overflow — it *garbles* the sidebar and status bar, because they're drawn at the stale width's absolute columns. In a real session the sidebar showed:

- dropped letters: `Host client` → `H s client`, `local + remote backend` → `l cal + remote back nd`
- a token counter split across rows with digits at every-2-column positions, e.g. `\x1b[6;201H 9`, `\x1b[6;203H 8`, `\x1b[6;205H 3`
- the status-bar cwd `/home/lenovo/ai-remote-hub` drawn as `[49;4H /home/lenovo/a` + `[49;19H -r` + `[49;22H mote-hub` (columns 18 and 21 never written)

All of it is in the raw PTY output — the terminal emulator and transport relay it faithfully. It develops over time (prompts + session switches = resizes), never on the welcome screen.

**Workaround confirmed + automated:** injecting Ctrl+L (`\x0c`) into the PTY after each geometry change forces opencode to repaint at the freshly-applied size and clears the garble every time. We shipped that server-side for our `opencode` sessions and it resolves it reliably.

Impact: this hits any deployment embedding opencode in a browser/web PTY (xterm.js, hterm, VS Code web, tmate-style bridges), and "shrink" happens constantly there (tab switches, keyboard, resize). A maintainer fix to re-layout on shrink / initial attach would be very welcome — happy to provide more trace data.

## Confirmation: systemic on Windows with oh-my-openagent plugin

We're seeing this on **v1.18.18** on Windows with the `oh-my-openagent` plugin. The bug is **not occasional** — it affects **every single child/subagent session** in our database.

### Evidence from DB inspection

The opencode SQLite DB (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, 10.3 GB) contains:

- **1,975 total sessions** across 5 projects (April 2026 – August 2026)
- **1,529 child sessions** (sessions with `parent_id IS NOT NULL`) — **all 1,529 have 0 rows in `session_message`**
- The `message` table has **64,561 rows** and the `part` table has **251,923 rows** — the data IS persisted, just not linked via `session_message`

For example, an Oracle review subagent session `ses_00587af5dffeYxgt0Z7syUy5sp`:
- `session_message` rows: **0**
- `part` rows: **111** (17 distinct `message_id`s)
- Those 17 `message_id`s all exist in the `message` table with correct `session_id` — the data is there, just the projection/join table is empty

### User-visible symptom

In the TUI, clicking on any subagent session shows only the handover prompt (the parent agent's message with the model name) — no subagent conversation, tool calls, reasoning, or response. This makes every subagent session look like a failure, even when the work completed successfully and the parent agent received the result.

### DB-level workaround

We repaired all 1,529 broken sessions by reconstructing `session_message` rows from existing `part` and `message` data:

```sql
-- For each broken session, get distinct message_ids from parts (ordered by creation time)
-- and insert session_message rows with sequential seq values
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO session_message (id, session_id, type, time_created, time_updated, data, seq)
SELECT p.message_id, p.session_id, 'message', 
       MIN(p.time_created), MAX(p.time_updated), 
       COALESCE(m.data, '{}'), 
       -- seq assigned per-session in application code
FROM part p
LEFT JOIN message m ON m.id = p.message_id
WHERE p.session_id = ? AND p.message_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.message_id
```

After this repair, the TUI correctly displays the full conversation history for all subagent sessions.

### Key observation

The `session_message.seq` column is `NOT NULL` with no default. If the projection insert fails (due to a null `seq` from a race condition or missing event sequence), the entire message-to-session link is lost silently. The message and part data are written independently and survive — only the projection fails.

This suggests the fix should ensure either:
1. `seq` has a safe default or is computed before insert (not dependent on an event that may be null), or
2. The insert failure is caught and retried with a computed `seq`, or
3. The TUI falls back to querying `part.message_id → message` directly when `session_message` is empty for a session that has parts
This is a really, really good feature. Users should be allowed to turn it on/off via Settings tho.

Correction to my earlier comment: I claimed injecting Ctrl+L after resizes resolves it reliably — that did **not** hold up on opencode 1.18.18. Measured against a live session:

- sending `\x0c` (Ctrl+L) into the PTY produces **zero bytes of output** — opencode ignores the unbound key entirely, no repaint happens
- Ctrl+P (command palette) does trigger a full re-render, but it re-renders **at the stale width**: after shrinking the PTY to 150 cols the redraw still draws at columns 197–230, so the sidebar/status stay wrong
- the welcome/first screen does re-layout correctly on shrink, but the full conversation view does not

So an input-injected workaround won't work in 1.18.18 — the TUI needs to actually re-read its size and re-layout on SIGWINCH (or a real terminal redraw), not just get a keystroke. Only restarting the session reliably recovers it. This looks like the more general form of #42225 (no re-layout on shrink), so fixing it properly is worth it — happy to provide the capture data.

> This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
> 
> * [Orphaned index.lock in snapshot gitdir causes blocking snapshot queue on Windows (Git Bash / mintty) #29413](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/29413): Similar symptom of an orphaned `.git/index.lock` left by opencode that cannot be removed without manual intervention. That issue focuses on the snapshot gitdir on Windows, but the root cause (opencode leaving a stale lock and holding git-related directory fds open) overlaps with what you describe here.
> 
> If your issue is specifically about the **user repo's** `.git/index.lock` being unremovable due to opencode keeping the `.git` directory open as a file descriptor (rather than the internal snapshot gitdir), it is likely a distinct but related bug and worth tracking separately.

Here is a clear, concise summary in English stating that the issues are analogous but not identical:

---

**The two issues are analogous but not identical.**

Both involve OpenCode leaving behind orphaned/stale `.git/index.lock` files, which then block subsequent Git operations and degrade performance. However, they differ in several key aspects:

- **#29413** occurs on **Windows** (Git Bash/mintty), affects OpenCode's **internal snapshot repository**, and is triggered by **abrupt process termination** (closing the terminal, Ctrl+C). The lock file causes the snapshot queue to hang, making OpenCode appear frozen.

- **actual** occurs on **macOS** (encrypted APFS volumes), affects the **user's working repository**, and is caused by **OpenCode holding open file descriptors** on the `.git` directory, which prevents the OS from removing the lock file (resulting in `EBUSY`). This makes manual Git commands fail.

In short: **same symptom (stale index.lock), same underlying category of problem (poor lock handling), but different environments, locations, and trigger mechanisms.** They are related but distinct bugs.

Current `dev` emits every completed text part from `run --format json` before resolving the owning message, while the compaction marker lives on that message rather than the part.

For the JSONL contract, should the fix (a) suppress compaction-summary and synthetic-continuation text entirely, preserving the existing event schema, or (b) emit a distinct control/compaction event with owner metadata? I lean toward (a) because these parts are not user-visible assistant output and it avoids expanding the public stream schema, but the intended compatibility contract needs confirmation before implementation.

The report confirms that `opencode2` currently opens and migrates the same database as stable 1.x, but the repository docs and V2 specs do not state whether side-by-side use is supported.

Is the intended contract that preview and stable may coexist? If yes, migrations need to preserve 1.x readability (or use a compatible copy); if no, should `opencode2` isolate its data/state namespace by default and warn before touching an existing stable database? That product/compatibility decision determines the correct fix and regression tests.

The failing path is OpenTUI's `SIGWINCH` debounce retaining cached `stdout` dimensions when the signal arrives before the runtime cache reflects the new PTY size. This also fixes a second, separately-reported symptom, which may be worth calling out in the description: with `=== "primary"` the ACP session ignores `default_agent` entirely.

The mechanism is narrower than it first looks. The server's agent list is already sorted with `default_agent` first, so the configured default sits at index 0 — it fails *only* the mode test. Config-defined agents are commonly `mode: all`, `=== "primary"` rejects `all`, so the search walks the whole custom roster and matches the built-in `build`, which is genuinely `primary`. Every ACP session therefore lands in `build` no matter what `default_agent` says.

Verified against `opencode serve` on 1.18.18 with a 30-agent config where all custom agents are `mode: all`, replaying both predicates over the real `GET /agent` payload:

```
agents returned: 30    first = Algorithm (mode=all)

  1.18.18   defaultModeID -> build
  this PR   defaultModeID -> Algorithm
```

Since the default happens to sort first alphabetically there, I re-ran with `default_agent: Writer` to rule out the alphabet:

```
first 5: Writer, Algorithm, Architect, Artist, Browser
  1.18.18 -> build
  this PR -> Writer
```

So `mode !== "subagent"` is exactly the relaxation `default_agent` needs, and the only local workaround without this PR is spelling the default agent `mode: primary` in frontmatter — which costs it `Task` subagent dispatchability, since `all` is what grants both roles. Not a trade users should have to make.

One review note on the approach, offered as a robustness point rather than a blocker: the new code still finds the default agent *positionally* (first non-subagent, non-hidden) rather than asking for it, so it depends on that sort order staying put. Two files over, `directory.ts` resolves the same thing explicitly via `agent.defaultInfo()`. Reusing that here would make the ACP path say what it means and stop a future change to the list ordering from silently reintroducing this bug.
